title: Uzbekistan Announces 30-Day Visa-Free Entry for Indian Travellers
excerpt: The visa waiver, announced during PM Modi's state visit, eliminates the previous e-visa requirement and comes alongside a UPI payment agreement for Indian travelers in Uzbekistan.
body:
• Uzbekistan has introduced a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens, announced during PM Modi's state visit on Aug. 29-30
  • A UPI payment agreement will allow Indian travelers to use UPI apps for transactions across Uzbekistan
  • Bilateral trade between the two countries exceeded $1 billion for the first time last year, with joint ventures increasing sevenfold
  • A Tourism Cooperation Programme for 2026-2028 includes plans for cultural weeks, film festivals, and joint tourist routes

Indian passport holders can now visit Uzbekistan without a visa for up to 30 days, under a new regime announced during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit to Tashkent on Aug. 29-30.

The move eliminates the previous requirement for Indian tourists to obtain an e-visa or sticker visa and marks a significant easing of travel between the two countries. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev made the announcement alongside Modi during bilateral talks.

"The introduction of a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens will make a significant contribution to the development of people-to-people contacts, tourism, and business exchanges."

— Shavkat Mirziyoyev, President of Uzbekistan

What the Agreement Covers

Beyond visa-free travel, the two nations signed a Tourism Cooperation Programme for 2026-2028 that includes reciprocal cultural weeks, film festivals, and jointly developed tourist routes. In a move particularly relevant for Indian travelers, the National Payments Corporation of India International and Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Centre signed a UPI payment agreement, which will allow Indians to use UPI apps for transactions in Uzbekistan once implemented.

There are currently 14 direct flights operating between India and Uzbekistan every week, providing established connectivity for travelers looking to take advantage of the new visa-free arrangement.

Why Uzbekistan Matters for Indian Travelers

Uzbekistan sits at the crossroads of the ancient Silk Road, and its cities of Samarkand, Bukhara, and Khiva are UNESCO World Heritage sites that have drawn travelers for centuries. The country already has cultural touchpoints with India — the Lal Bahadur Shastri Center for Indian Culture and the Mahatma Gandhi Center for Indian Studies are established institutions, and a yoga federation has operated in Uzbekistan since 2018.

The visa-free move brings Uzbekistan in line with its Central Asian neighbors Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, which already offer visa-free entry to Indian citizens. For NRIs in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, the announcement opens up easier access to Silk Road heritage destinations on their Indian passports without navigating an additional visa process.

Deepening Economic Ties

The tourism agreement comes against a backdrop of rapidly growing economic relations. Bilateral trade between India and Uzbekistan exceeded $1 billion for the first time last year, and the number of joint ventures between the two countries has increased sevenfold in recent years. Mirziyoyev described India as a "reliable strategic partner" during the summit.

The growing corridor also reflects India's broader strategic engagement with Central Asia. Modi's state visit — the first by an Indian prime minister to Uzbekistan since 2018 — underscored the priority both governments are placing on strengthening ties beyond traditional diplomatic channels.

Travelers should check official updates from the Uzbekistan embassy or consulate for implementation timelines and specific entry requirements, as the announcement is newly made and procedural details may still be finalized.
